newsitem.title: USA: Fla. governor relieved at restored hurricane funds.
newsitem.headline: Fla. governor relieved at restored hurricane funds.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles Thursday called the Clinton administration's decision to restore funding for staffing at the National Hurricane Center "a significant victory"

In a letter to the Senate Appropriations Committee dated Thursday and distributed by the governor's office, U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley said the administration had decided "to reprogram $715,000" of funding, which will allow the maintenance of staffing at the National Hurricane Center at last year's level.

Residents of Florida and other coastal states have been up in arms since last month, when they learned that federal budget cuts would eliminate several jobs at the center, which monitors worldwide storm activity and is responsible for posting hurricane watches and warnings to coastal areas during the six-month Atlantic hurricane season.

"I'm delighted that Commerce Secretary Bill Daley will restore funding for staffing at the National Hurricane Center," Chiles said in a statement. "This decision is a significant victory for the people of Florida -- and for Americans from Texas to Maine."

Frank Lapore, a spokesman from the National Hurricane Center, said the funds would help. "In addition to getting the six people back, that means that we would be able to turn out the full array of forecasting products we produce," he said.

But he said reaction at the forecasting station outside Miami had been moderate, noting that the funding restores six positions only until the end of the fiscal year, Sept. 30, while the hurricane season ends Nov. 30.
"It's a short-term fix," he said, noting that it also does not address $10 million in funding for 1998 needed for maintenance, supplies and training.

In the letter, Daley said the funding was available because of the National Oceanographic and Atmospheric Administration's decision to reduce some funding to the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
He also said staffing needs at the National Hurricane Center and other national forecasting centers would be evaluated at the Nov. 30 end of the 1997 hurricane season.
